sanskrit: na viśvased aviśvaste viśvaste nātiviśvaset viśvāsād bhayam utpannaṃ mūlāny api nikṛntati
english: One should not trust the untrustworthy, nor should one trust the trustworthy too absolutely; for fear born of misplaced trust cuts even roots asunder.

sanskrit: anīrṣyur guptadāraḥ syāt saṃvibhāgī priyaṃvadaḥ ślakṣṇo madhuravāk strīṇāṃ na cāsāṃ vaśago bhavet
english: A man should be free from jealousy, guard his wife, be generous, speak pleasantly, be gentle and sweet-spoken toward women, yet never be enslaved by them.

sanskrit: pūjanīyā mahābhāgāḥ puṇyāś ca gṛhadīptayaḥ striyaḥ śriyo gṛhasyoktās tasmād rakṣyā viśeṣataḥ
english: Women are said to be the Lakṣmī of the household — greatly fortunate, holy, and the very light of the home; therefore they are to be protected with especial care.

sanskrit: pitur antaḥpuraṃ dadyān mātur dadyān mahānasam goṣu cātmasamaṃ dadyāt svayam eva kṛṣiṃ vrajet bhṛtyair vaṇijyācāraṃ ca putraiḥ seveta brāhmaṇān
english: One should entrust the inner apartments to the father, the kitchen to the mother, and the cattle to one equal to oneself; one should personally oversee agriculture, conduct trade through servants, and honor Brahmins through one's sons.

sanskrit: adbhyo 'gnir brahmataḥ kṣatram aśmano loham utthitam teṣāṃ sarvatragaṃ tejaḥ svāsu yoniṣu śāmyati
english: Fire arises from water, the Kṣatriya from Brahman, and iron from stone; the all-pervading energy of each is quenched in its own origin.

sanskrit: nityaṃ santaḥ kule jātāḥ pāvakopamatejasaḥ kṣamāvanto nirākārāḥ kāṣṭhe 'gnir iva śerate
english: The good who are born in noble families, blazing like fire, yet patient and without outward display, lie dormant like fire hidden within wood.

sanskrit: yasya mantraṃ na jānanti bāhyāś cābhyantarāś ca ye sa rājā sarvataścakṣuś ciram aiśvaryam aśnute
english: That king whose counsel is unknown to both outsiders and those within his own circle — he who sees in all directions — enjoys sovereignty for a long time.

sanskrit: kariṣyan na prabhāṣeta kṛtāny eva ca darśayet dharmakāmārthakāryāṇi tathā mantro na bhidyate
english: One should not speak of what one is about to do, but display what has already been accomplished; when matters of dharma, desire, and wealth are kept thus, counsel remains unbroken.

sanskrit: giripṛṣṭham upāruhya prāsādaṃ vā rahogataḥ araṇye niḥśalāke vā tatra mantro vidhīyate
english: Counsel should be taken on the summit of a mountain, in a secluded palace chamber, or in a forest free of stakes and thorns — in such private places.

sanskrit: nāsuhṛt paramaṃ mantraṃ bhāratārhati veditum apaṇḍito vāpi suhṛt paṇḍito vāpy anātmavān amātye hy arthalipsā ca mantrarakṣaṇam eva ca
english: A non-friend does not deserve to know the highest counsel, O descendant of Bharata; nor does an unwise friend, nor a wise man lacking self-control; for in a minister both the desire for gain and the safeguarding of counsel must coexist.

sanskrit: kṛtāni sarvakāryāṇi yasya vā pārṣadā viduḥ gūḍhamantrasya nṛpates tasya siddhir asaṃśayam
english: For that king whose counselors know all affairs already concluded — that king who keeps his deliberations secret — success is without doubt.

sanskrit: apraśastāni karmāṇi yo mohād anutiṣṭhati sa teṣāṃ viparibhraṃśe bhraśyate jīvitād api
english: He who through delusion pursues ignoble deeds, when those deeds recoil upon him, falls from life itself.

sanskrit: karmaṇāṃ tu praśastānām anuṣṭhānaṃ sukhāvaham teṣām evānanuṣṭhānaṃ paścāttāpakaraṃ mahat
english: The performance of praiseworthy actions brings happiness; the non-performance of those very same actions causes great remorse thereafter.

sanskrit: sthānavṛddhikṣayajñasya ṣāḍguṇyaviditātmanaḥ anavajñātaśīlasya svādhīnā pṛthivī nṛpa
english: For the king who knows the increase and decline of positions, who understands the six royal policies and knows his own self, and whose conduct is never held in contempt — the earth is under his sway, O king.

sanskrit: amoghakrodhaharṣasya svayaṃ kṛtyānvavekṣiṇaḥ ātmapratyayakośasya vasudheyaṃ vasuṃdharā
english: For him whose anger and joy are never in vain, who personally supervises his own duties, and whose treasury is under his own control — the earth becomes a giver of wealth.

sanskrit: nāmamātreṇa tuṣyeta chatreṇa ca mahīpatiḥ bhṛtyebhyo visṛjed arthān naikaḥ sarvaharo bhavet
english: A lord of the earth should not be satisfied with mere name and royal umbrella; he should distribute wealth among his servants and not be the sole taker of everything.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo brāhmaṇaṃ veda bhartā veda striyaṃ tathā amātyaṃ nṛpatir veda rājā rājānam eva ca
english: A Brahmin knows a Brahmin; a husband knows his wife; a king knows his minister; and a king knows another king.

sanskrit: na śatrur aṅkam āpanno moktavyo vadhyatāṃ gataḥ ahatād dhi bhayaṃ tasmāj jāyate nacirād iva
english: An enemy who has fallen into one's lap and is fit for destruction should not be released; for from one who has not been slain, fear arises again very soon.

sanskrit: daivateṣu ca yatnena rājasu brāhmaṇeṣu ca niyantavyaḥ sadā krodho vṛddhabālātureṣu ca
english: Anger should always be carefully restrained toward the gods, toward kings, toward Brahmins, and toward the aged, children, and the sick.

sanskrit: nirarthaṃ kalahaṃ prājño varjayen mūḍhasevitam kīrtiṃ ca labhate loke na cānarthena yujyate
english: A wise man avoids pointless quarrel, which is the practice of fools; thereby he gains fame in the world and is not joined to calamity.

sanskrit: prasādo niṣphalo yasya krodhaś cāpi nirarthakaḥ na taṃ bhartāram icchanti ṣaṇḍhaṃ patim iva striyaḥ
english: He whose grace yields no fruit and whose anger too is purposeless — servants do not desire such a master, just as women do not desire an impotent husband.

sanskrit: na buddhir dhanalābhāya na jāḍyam asamṛddhaye lokaparyāyavṛttāntaṃ prājño jānāti netaraḥ
english: Intellect alone does not bring wealth, nor does dullness alone lead to poverty; the wise man understands the cyclic turns of the world's affairs — others do not.

sanskrit: vidyāśīlavayovṛddhān buddhivṛddhāṃś ca bhārata dhanābhijanavṛddhāṃś ca nityaṃ mūḍho 'vamanyate
english: A fool always disregards those great in learning, character, and age, those great in wisdom, and those great in wealth and lineage, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: anāryavṛttam aprājñam asūyakam adhārmikam anarthāḥ kṣipram āyānti vāgduṣṭaṃ krodhanaṃ tathā
english: Misfortunes swiftly come to him who behaves ignobly, who is unwise, envious, unrighteous, foul-tongued, and wrathful.

sanskrit: avisaṃvādanaṃ dānaṃ samayasyāvyatikramaḥ āvartayanti bhūtāni samyak praṇihitā ca vāk
english: Non-deception, generosity, not violating agreements, and speech that is properly directed — these turn living beings back toward one in good will.

sanskrit: avisaṃvādako dakṣaḥ kṛtajño matimān ṛjuḥ api saṃkṣīṇakośo 'pi labhate parivāraṇam
english: One who does not deceive, who is capable, grateful, intelligent, and straightforward — even if his treasury is diminished — still gains a following.

sanskrit: dhṛtiḥ śamo damaḥ śaucaṃ kāruṇyaṃ vāg aniṣṭhurā mitrāṇāṃ cānabhidrohaḥ saptaitāḥ samidhaḥ śriyaḥ
english: Fortitude, tranquility, self-restraint, purity, compassion, speech that is not harsh, and non-betrayal of friends — these seven are the fuel-sticks of prosperity.

sanskrit: asaṃvibhāgī duṣṭātmā kṛtaghno nirapatrapaḥ tādṛṅ narādhamo loke varjanīyo narādhipa
english: One who does not share, who is wicked at heart, ungrateful, and shameless — such a basest of men is to be shunned in this world, O lord of men.

sanskrit: na sa rātrau sukhaṃ śete sasarpa iva veśmani yaḥ kopayati nirdoṣaṃ sadoṣo 'bhyantaraṃ janam
english: He who, being himself at fault, angers blameless members of his own household, does not sleep in peace at night — like one whose house contains a serpent.

sanskrit: yeṣu duṣṭeṣu doṣaḥ syād yogakṣemasya bhārata sadā prasādanaṃ teṣāṃ devatānām ivācaret
english: Those whose enmity would threaten one's prosperity and security, O Bhārata — one should always propitiate them as one propitiates the gods.

sanskrit: ye 'rthāḥ strīṣu samāsaktāḥ prathamotpatiteṣu ca ye cānāryasamāsaktāḥ sarve te saṃśayaṃ gatāḥ
english: Wealth that is entrusted to women, wealth placed in the hands of those newly risen, and wealth dependent on the ignoble — all such wealth is in a state of uncertainty.

sanskrit: yatra strī yatra kitavo yatra bālo 'nuśāsti ca majjanti te 'vaśā deśā nadyām aśmaplavā iva
english: Where a woman rules, where a gambler rules, where a child gives commands — those lands sink helplessly, like stones in a river.

sanskrit: prayojaneṣu ye saktā na viśeṣeṣu bhārata tān ahaṃ paṇḍitān manye viśeṣā hi prasaṅginaḥ
english: Those who are devoted to essential purposes and not to outward distinctions, O Bhārata — those I consider truly wise; for distinctions are the province of attachment.

sanskrit: yaṃ praśaṃsanti kitavā yaṃ praśaṃsanti cāraṇāḥ yaṃ praśaṃsanti bandhakyo na sa jīvati mānavaḥ
english: The man whom gamblers praise, whom wandering bards praise, whom prostitutes praise — such a man does not truly live.

sanskrit: hitvā tān parameṣvāsān pāṇḍavān amitaujasaḥ āhitaṃ bhārataiśvaryaṃ tvayā duryodhane mahat
english: Having abandoned those supreme archers, the Pāṇḍavas of boundless might, you have placed the great sovereignty of the Bhāratas in Duryodhana's hands.

sanskrit: taṃ drakṣyasi paribhraṣṭaṃ tasmāt tvaṃ nacirād iva aiśvaryamadasaṃmūḍhaṃ baliṃ lokatrayād iva
english: You will very soon see him fallen from that sovereignty — him who is stupefied by the pride of power — just as Bali was cast down from the three worlds.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca anīśvaro 'yaṃ puruṣo bhavābhave; sūtraprotā dārumayīva yoṣā dhātrā tu diṣṭasya vaśe kilāyaṃ; tasmād vada tvaṃ śravaṇe dhṛto 'ham
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: This man is not his own master in prosperity or adversity; like a wooden doll strung on threads, he is subject to the ordainer's decree of fate. Therefore, speak — I am attentive, all ears.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca aprāptakālaṃ vacanaṃ bṛhaspatir api bruvan labhate buddhyavajñānam avamānaṃ ca bhārata
english: Vidura said: Even Bṛhaspati, if he speaks at the wrong moment, receives only contempt for his wisdom and disrespect, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: priyo bhavati dānena priyavādena cāparaḥ mantraṃ mūlabalenānyo yaḥ priyaḥ priya eva saḥ
english: One person becomes dear through giving, another through pleasant speech, another through the strength of counsel and fundamental support; he who is dear in that last way is truly dear.

sanskrit: dveṣyo na sādhur bhavati na medhāvī na paṇḍitaḥ priye śubhāni karmāṇi dveṣye pāpāni bhārata
english: One who is disliked does not appear virtuous, intelligent, or learned; to one who is loved, auspicious deeds are attributed; to one who is disliked, evil ones, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: na sa kṣayo mahārāja yaḥ kṣayo vṛddhim āvahet kṣayaḥ sa tv iha mantavyo yaṃ labdhvā bahu nāśayet
english: That is not truly a loss, O great king, which brings growth in its wake; what should be regarded as true loss here is that which, once suffered, destroys much more.

sanskrit: samṛddhā guṇataḥ ke cid bhavanti dhanato 'pare dhanavṛddhān guṇair hīnān dhṛtarāṣṭra vivarjayet
english: Some are prosperous in virtue, others in wealth; those who are rich in wealth but poor in virtue — avoid them, O Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca sarvaṃ tvam āyatīyuktaṃ bhāṣase prājñasaṃmatam na cotsahe sutaṃ tyaktuṃ yato dharmas tato jayaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: All that you speak is fitting for the future and is approved by the wise; yet I have not the heart to abandon my son. Where there is dharma, there is victory.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca svabhāvaguṇasaṃpanno na jātu vinayānvitaḥ susūkṣmam api bhūtānām upamardaṃ prayokṣyate
english: Vidura said: One who is endowed with natural virtue and imbued with humility will never inflict even the slightest harm upon any living being.

sanskrit: parāpavādaniratāḥ paraduḥkhodayeṣu ca parasparavirodhe ca yatante satatotthitāḥ
english: There are those who are devoted to slandering others, who delight when others suffer misfortune, and who are always striving to create mutual discord among people.

sanskrit: sadoṣaṃ darśanaṃ yeṣāṃ saṃvāse sumahad bhayam arthādāne mahān doṣaḥ pradāne ca mahad bhayam
english: Those whose very sight is tainted with fault, in whose company there is immense fear, whose taking of wealth is full of vice, and whose giving is also fraught with great danger —

sanskrit: ye pāpā iti vikhyātāḥ saṃvāse parigarhitāḥ yuktāś cānyair mahādoṣair ye narās tān vivarjayet
english: Those men who are notorious as sinful, who are reproached in society, and who are tainted by other grave faults — such men one should avoid.

sanskrit: nivartamāne sauhārde prītir nīce praṇaśyati yā caiva phalanirvṛttiḥ sauhṛde caiva yat sukham
english: When friendship with a base person wanes, the affection vanishes; and so too does the fulfillment of results from that friendship, and whatever joy existed in that bond.

sanskrit: yatate cāpavādāya yatnam ārabhate kṣaye alpe 'py apakṛte mohān na śāntim upagacchati
english: Such a person strives to defame others and makes effort toward their destruction; even when the wrong done is slight, he does not, out of delusion, find peace.

sanskrit: tādṛśaiḥ saṃgataṃ nīcair nṛśaṃsair akṛtātmabhiḥ niśāmya nipuṇaṃ buddhyā vidvān dūrād vivarjayet
english: Having carefully observed with discerning intelligence such base, cruel, and uncontrolled persons, a learned man should avoid them from afar.

sanskrit: yo jñātim anugṛhṇāti daridraṃ dīnam āturam sa putrapaśubhir vṛddhiṃ yaśaś cāvyayam aśnute
english: He who supports a kinsman who is poor, wretched, or afflicted — he gains prosperity in sons and cattle, and imperishable fame.

sanskrit: jñātayo vardhanīyās tair ya icchanty ātmanaḥ śubham kulavṛddhiṃ ca rājendra tasmāt sādhu samācara
english: Kinsmen should be nurtured by those who desire their own welfare and the growth of their family, O lord of kings; therefore conduct yourself well.

sanskrit: śreyasā yokṣyase rājan kurvāṇo jñātisatkriyām viguṇā hy api saṃrakṣyā jñātayo bharatarṣabha
english: By honoring your kinsmen you will be united with what is best, O king; even kinsmen who are lacking in virtue must be protected, O bull among the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: kiṃ punar guṇavantas te tvatprasādābhikāṅkṣiṇaḥ prasādaṃ kuru dīnānāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ viśāṃ pate
english: How much more so then, when they are virtuous and yearn for your grace? Show grace to the afflicted Pāṇḍavas, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: dīyantāṃ grāmakāḥ ke cit teṣāṃ vṛttyartham īśvara evaṃ loke yaśaḥprāpto bhaviṣyasi narādhipa
english: Grant them some villages for their livelihood, O lord; by doing so you will attain fame in this world, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: vṛddhena hi tvayā kāryaṃ putrāṇāṃ tāta rakṣaṇam mayā cāpi hitaṃ vācyaṃ viddhi māṃ tvaddhitaiṣiṇam
english: For you, as an elder, the protection of your sons is your duty, dear one; and by me too what is beneficial must be spoken — know me to be one who desires your good.

sanskrit: jñātibhir vigrahas tāta na kartavyo bhavārthinā sukhāni saha bhojyāni jñātibhir bharatarṣabha
english: Conflict with kinsmen should not be made by one who desires prosperity, dear one; pleasures are to be enjoyed together with one's kinsmen, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: saṃbhojanaṃ saṃkathanaṃ saṃprītiś ca parasparam jñātibhiḥ saha kāryāṇi na virodhaḥ kathaṃ cana
english: Eating together, conversing together, and mutual affection — these are the things to be done with kinsmen; conflict with them should never occur under any circumstances.

sanskrit: jñātayas tārayantīha jñātayo majjayanti ca suvṛttās tārayantīha durvṛttā majjayanti ca
english: Kinsmen can uplift in this world, and kinsmen can cause one to sink; those of good conduct uplift, while those of bad conduct cause one to sink.

sanskrit: suvṛtto bhava rājendra pāṇḍavān prati mānada adharṣaṇīyaḥ śatrūṇāṃ tair vṛtas tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi
english: Conduct yourself well toward the Pāṇḍavas, O lord of kings, O bestower of honor; surrounded by them, you will be invincible to your enemies.

sanskrit: śrīmantaṃ jñātim āsādya yo jñātir avasīdati digdhahastaṃ mṛga iva sa enas tasya vindati
english: The kinsman who, though near a prosperous kinsman, still sinks into misery — he incurs that prosperous kinsman's sin, like a deer caught by one whose hand is smeared with poison.

sanskrit: paścād api naraśreṣṭha tava tāpo bhaviṣyati tān vā hatān sutān vāpi śrutvā tad anucintaya
english: You will grieve afterward, O best of men, upon hearing that they have been slain or that your own sons have been slain — reflect on this now.

sanskrit: yena khaṭvāṃ samārūḍhaḥ paritapyeta karmaṇā ādāv eva na tat kuryād adhruve jīvite sati
english: The action on account of which, lying on his deathbed, a man would be tormented — that action he should not do from the very beginning, given the uncertainty of life.

sanskrit: na kaś cin nāpanayate pumān anyatra bhārgavāt śeṣasaṃpratipattis tu buddhimatsv eva tiṣṭhati
english: There is no man who does not commit some wrong act, save Bhārgava alone; but the remedy for what remains — the capacity to set right — rests only in the wise.

sanskrit: duryodhanena yady etat pāpaṃ teṣu purā kṛtam tvayā tat kulavṛddhena pratyāneyaṃ nareśvara
english: If that sin was done to the Pāṇḍavas earlier by Duryodhana, then it is for you, O lord of men, as the elder of the family, to remedy it.

sanskrit: tāṃs tvaṃ pade pratiṣṭhāpya loke vigatakalmaṣaḥ bhaviṣyasi naraśreṣṭha pūjanīyo manīṣiṇām
english: By restoring them to their rightful position, you will be free of sin in this world, O best of men, and worthy of worship by the wise.

sanskrit: suvyāhṛtāni dhīrāṇāṃ phalataḥ pravicintya yaḥ adhyavasyati kāryeṣu ciraṃ yaśasi tiṣṭhati
english: He who, having carefully reflected on the well-spoken words of the steadfast and their fruits, determines his course of action accordingly — such a man abides long in glory.

sanskrit: avṛttiṃ vinayo hanti hanty anarthaṃ parākramaḥ hanti nityaṃ kṣamā krodham ācāro hanty alakṣaṇam
english: Humility destroys poverty; valor destroys calamity; forbearance always destroys anger; and right conduct destroys ill-omened qualities.

sanskrit: paricchadena kṣetreṇa veśmanā paricaryayā parīkṣeta kulaṃ rājan bhojanācchādanena ca
english: By one's retinue, one's field, one's dwelling, one's service, and by one's food and clothing — from these can a family's true nature be assessed, O king.

sanskrit: yayoś cittena vā cittaṃ naibhṛtaṃ naibhṛtena vā sameti prajñayā prajñā tayor maitrī na jīryate
english: Between those two whose minds meet mind to mind in quietness and whose wisdom meets wisdom — the friendship between them does not decay.

sanskrit: durbuddhim akṛtaprajñaṃ channaṃ kūpaṃ tṛṇair iva vivarjayīta medhāvī tasmin maitrī praṇaśyati
english: A man of intelligence should avoid one of wicked understanding and undeveloped wisdom, as one avoids a well covered with grass; friendship with such a person perishes.

sanskrit: avalipteṣu mūrkheṣu raudrasāhasikeṣu ca tathaivāpetadharmeṣu na maitrīm ācared budhaḥ
english: With the arrogant, the foolish, the violently reckless, and those who have abandoned dharma — a wise man should not cultivate friendship.

sanskrit: kṛtajñaṃ dhārmikaṃ satyam akṣudraṃ dṛḍhabhaktikam jitendriyaṃ sthitaṃ sthityāṃ mitram atyāgi ceṣyate
english: A friend who is grateful, righteous, truthful, not mean-spirited, of firm devotion, master of his senses, steadfast in his steadfastness, and who never abandons — such a one is a desired friend.

sanskrit: indriyāṇām anutsargo mṛtyunā na viśiṣyate atyarthaṃ punar utsargaḥ sādayed daivatāny api
english: Total suppression of the senses is no different from death; but excessive indulgence of them could afflict even the gods.

sanskrit: mārdavaṃ sarvabhūtānām anasūyā kṣamā dhṛtiḥ āyuṣyāṇi budhāḥ prāhur mitrāṇāṃ cāvimānanā
english: Gentleness toward all beings, freedom from envy, forbearance, firmness, and not disrespecting friends — these the wise declare to be life-prolonging virtues.

sanskrit: apanītaṃ sunītena yo 'rthaṃ pratyāninīṣate matim āsthāya sudṛḍhāṃ tad akāpuruṣavratam
english: He who, through skillful policy, seeks to recover what was lost through poor policy, by taking firm and resolute counsel — that is the vow of a true man, not a coward.

sanskrit: āyatyāṃ pratikārajñas tadātve dṛḍhaniścayaḥ atīte kāryaśeṣajño naro 'rthair na prahīyate
english: The man who knows how to remedy future adversity, who is firm in resolve in the present moment, and who knows what remains to be done when past affairs are concluded — such a man is not abandoned by fortune.

sanskrit: karmaṇā manasā vācā yad abhīkṣṇaṃ niṣevate tad evāpaharaty enaṃ tasmāt kalyāṇam ācaret
english: Whatever one constantly practices in deed, thought, and speech — that very thing carries one away; therefore one should practice what is auspicious.

sanskrit: maṅgalālambhanaṃ yogaḥ śrutam utthānam ārjavam bhūtim etāni kurvanti satāṃ cābhīkṣṇadarśanam
english: Resorting to auspicious things, disciplined practice, learning, diligence, straightforwardness, and the constant company of the virtuous — these bring prosperity.

sanskrit: anirvedaḥ śriyo mūlaṃ duḥkhanāśe sukhasya ca mahān bhavaty anirviṇṇaḥ sukhaṃ cātyantam aśnute
english: Non-despondency is the root of prosperity and of the destruction of sorrow and the arising of joy; the one who is never disheartened becomes great and attains supreme happiness.
